correctness.rationale: Exact rational calculations from displayed map give E=(3/2,3/2) with eigenvalues 2/5 and -438/455, and F(A)=B, F(B)=A for A=(2,2/3), B=(2/3,2). The exact return Jacobian satisfies all three strict Schur inequalities (1-T+det=423302/3583125; 1+T+det=209855777/93161250; 1-det=16864819/20702500), so both sink types persist under small admissible C1 perturbations. Strict increase of g(z)=5z/[2(1+z)] and its global scalar attraction give the constant-dispersal impossibility by bounding each coordinate between g iterates of initial min and max. Exact identities recomputed from package verify_exact.py; finite checks are not substitutes for analytic persistence/convergence proofs.

value.rationale: The sharp qualitative boundary of a natural Beverton–Holt metapopulation stability result is that density-dependent costly emigration, without local overcompensation, Allee mechanisms, patch heterogeneity, or maturation delay, permits two simultaneously attracting long-term ecological regimes. Complete exact rational two-step stability certificates and robust continuation demonstrate more than a numerical periodicity plot or a routine local linearization. The contrast with any constant emigration fraction for the same surviving recruitment identifies genuinely causative state dependence.
